tools.name: list_datasets
tools.description: Every Aperiodic dataset, metrics and raw: id, category, the plan that unlocks it, a one-line description, field count, and whether this caller gets full access or the free preview. Start here.

tools.name: describe_dataset
tools.description: Field definitions, intervals, exchanges with their start dates, the plan needed and the free preview window for one dataset.

tools.name: find_symbols
tools.description: Symbol ids on one exchange matching every word of the query, at most 50. Ids look like "perpetual-BTC-USDT:USDT". The free preview symbol is perpetual-BTC-USDT:USDT on binance-futures.

tools.name: get_data
tools.description: A handle to one slice of a dataset, not the data: signed Parquet URLs (valid one hour), schema, row counts, per-column min/max/nulls from the Parquet footers, 5 sample rows and a Polars snippet. Load the files in your own code; never paste them into the conversation. Without code, use summarize. Eve

tools.name: summarize
tools.description: Statistics worked out on our side, for when you can't run code: per-column count, mean, std, quantiles and range ("stats"), a correlation matrix ("correlation"), or the series resampled to at most 500 points ("resample"). Same slice arguments and plan rules as get_data. Decodes only the columns you

tools.name: live_feed
tools.description: How your own code connects to the real-time WebSocket feed: its URL, the subscribe frame for a dataset, exchange, interval and symbols, your plan's limits and a Python client. Never the stream itself. With no dataset, lists what streams and which plans include it.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Keyword search over every dataset, its fields, the categories and the plans guide. Returns ids, titles and URLs; read one with fetch.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: The full text of one search result: a dataset with all its fields, a category, or the plans guide.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.
